payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: In the edited image, is the woman's jacket fully closed, with its front panels together and no visible opening remaining along the closure?
node.criteria: Pass: the jacket is visibly fully closed, with its front panels together and no opening along the closure. Fail: the jacket is visibly not fully closed, including any visible opening along the closure. Unknown: the closure or its full extent cannot be judged from the image.
node.binding: Directly inspect the requested endpoint in the edited image; the input image is context for identifying the woman's jacket, not a prerequisite for checking the endpoint.

fulfillment:
The node’s binding is truncated/ambiguous (`The jacket (...) jacket is closed completely`) and omits the explicit source-image target and observable closure cues. Repair it as a typed structural edit: bind to the woman’s jacket in the input image, and define the endpoint as fully closed with the front panels together and no visible opening. Preserve the separate progress comparison against the source; do not let evidence of an open jacket alone decide whether any requested progress occurred.

The traces consistently and confidently find the edited jacket visibly open, so completion is not supported. However, the source shows the woman facing forward while the edit turns her sideways and the jacket hangs away from her body; that viewpoint/pose change makes progress harder to compare, and one support correctly returns unknown. Treat this as an evidence/comparability issue, not a transport or schema failure, and do not convert uncertainty into a negative finding. Keep the rubric’s distinction between complete, partial, absent, and unresolved, with skipped or unobservable evidence remaining unobserved. The reference label constrains the aggregate but does not establish atomic truth; investigate the disagreement rather than forcing a yes or weakening the closure criterion.
s2: Repair the node’s binding so it explicitly identifies the same woman’s jacket in the source and edited images, and make the progress criterion compare observable closure cues across them (front-panel separation/gap and how much of the front is brought together). Keep the existing distinction: pass only for visible movement toward closure that remains incomplete; fail only when comparable evidence shows no progress; unknown when pose, occlusion, or viewpoint prevents a reliable comparison. In these images the edited jacket is still visibly open and hangs away from the body, while the woman has turned sideways; that supports lack of completion but makes progress harder to assess, so do not infer no progress merely from the remaining opening. Preserve uncertainty rather than forcing a label. The repeated valid traces are visual judgments, not transport/schema failures; investigate their disagreement with the aggregate reference without treating that reference as atomic ground truth or weakening the full-closure requirement.
